search_log: Searched “A Painted House John Grisham excerpt first chapter narrator,” “A Painted House first person narrator Luke Chandler,” and publisher- and author-domain variants.
Opened BookBrowse’s Doubleday-authorized Chapter I excerpt and confirmed sustained participating first-person narration.

Searched first-person-narrator and scholarly critical-analysis variants; opened Mary Beth Pringle’s whole-novel critical study and verified its publication metadata through Google Books, WorldCat, and Bloomsbury.

Searched “A Painted House alternating narrator multiple narrators,” “A Painted House epistolary frame narrative,” and ending/interior-excerpt variants; found no evidence of a different sustained base person.

Opened Penguin Random House product and reader-guide pages and Google Books metadata; they verified the work and its focus on Luke but were less directly person-diagnostic than the excerpt and critical study.
An initial PDF fetch of the Pringle study timed out, but its extracted HTML text was opened successfully; an unverified library full-text mirror was not used as evidence.
person_note: Luke Chandler is the controlling participating narrator, recounting the story as “I” and occasionally inclusive “we.” Fourteen dispersed quote passages directly expose that voice. The generic “you” in q00891 is not story-specific second person, the third-person descriptions are compatible with Luke narrating other characters, and q00903 is local speech. The authorized opening, a whole-book scholarly analysis, and two whole-book reviews independently agree on first-person narration, while targeted searches found no alternating, framed, diary, or epistolary structure. The authorized prose source covers only the opening, but the whole-book sources and numerous interior quote passages close that scope gap; no material uncertainty remains.
